registered: 2026-10-17 (committed to git BEFORE any of these indicators was used to evaluate forecasting models; before the Phase 7 red-team results were read)
question: Does any non-baseline CHRONOS forecasting model beat simple extrapolation on indicators, countries and periods that were never used to develop or evaluate it?
previously_used_for_model_evaluation: gdp_per_capita (owid): United States and the full country panel

holdout_indicators.description: CO2 per person (Global Carbon Budget via OWID)
average years of education (V-Dem external variable)
Seshat coded (not imputed) polity population, log10, century steps

entities: all entities of the indicator with an ISO3/NGA identity (OWID aggregates OWID_* excluded) whose regular tail run has >= 40 observations (annual) or >= 15 observations (century data); filler observations are never scored

models_frozen.note: analog models are annual-only; for century data only baselines + damped_trend are evaluated. No hyper-parameter may be changed after this registration.

origins: every 5 years (annual) / every century (Seshat) from the first origin with >= 25 (annual) or 10 (century) observations of history
primary_comparator: drift (window 20) — the best baseline in the earlier gdp_per_capita panel; fixed in advance, not chosen on the test data
primary_metric: scaled absolute error |y - yhat| / s, s = in-sample mean |y_t - y_{t-h}| at the origin (MASE terms), averaged over all (entity, origin) pairs common to the candidate and the comparator
decision_rule: A candidate 'beats' the comparator for an (indicator, horizon) cell only if the 95% CI of the mean scaled-error difference (candidate - comparator), from a bootstrap that resamples blocks of origin years (block length = horizon) jointly across all entities (2000 replications), lies entirely below 0 AND the result survives Holm correction across all candidate x indicator x horizon cells. Otherwise the result is recorded as 'no evidence of improvement'.
secondary: empirical 80% interval coverage of every model per cell (target 0.75-0.85)
share of entities in which the candidate has lower MAE (descriptive only)
reporting: All cells are reported, including failures and cells with too few entities (< 10 entities or < 30 forecasts => 'insufficient data'). Results go to MODEL_SCORECARD.md regardless of outcome.
